newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--blocked from rally by supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--blocked from rally by supply.

text.p: Despite a dramatic rise in both Treasuries and futures Tuesday, the cash market for U.S. municipal bonds managed only modest gains, burdened by the weight of heavy new issue calendars.
"There's a lot of supply and the market's already feeling on the heavy side," one trader said. "There are a lot of deals still coming to market, big deals, and a lock of real retail participation."

A market analyst judged the overall municipal market up only about 3/8 point, compared to a Treasury market where the long bond was up nearly two points at 100-27/32 to yield 6.68 percent, the lowest yield since April 4.
The Treasury market rallied sharply after a lower-than-expected employment cost index for the third quarter. The indicator rose 0.6 percent, instead of the 0.8 percent rise economists had predicted.
The report bolstered the view that the Federal Reserve may leave interest rates unchanged at its Nov. 13 meeting.
Active secondary muni bonds included Chicago O'Hare Airport AMBAC 5-1/2s of 2018. Bids fell seven basis points from Monday, to 6.05 percent net.
Yields droppped six basis points, to 5.71 percent net, on Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023. The yield stood at 5.74 percent at midday.
In futures, the December municipal contract closed up 1-1/32 at 115-1/32, while the December T-bond ended 1-22/32 higher at 112-19/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 78 ticks from 99 at the close Monday.
Among afternoon repricings, EVEREN Securities Inc said it repriced $134 million Chicago Park District bonds, adjusting yields in several maturities. The top yield was 5.92 percent in 2024.

The largest deal of the week came to market earlier in the day, when Smith Barney Inc tentatively priced $446 million North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency bonds at a top yield of approximately 5.958 percent in 2021.

Topping off the busy competitive calendar, JP Morgan Securities won $38.4 million Wisconsin certificates of participation and reoffered the bonds at yields from 3.70 percent in 1997 to 4.95 percent in 2003. To see the reoffering
Wednesday's negotiated deals total $1.1 billion, including a nearly $600 million New York State Urban Development Corp issue through PaineWebber Inc.

The competitive calendar total $392 million, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group. The week's largest competitive issue, a $133 million Virginia Public School Authority deal, is set for 1100 EST.
